title: Named Mainz, Olomouc, German, Hungarian, Adriatic, Utrecht and Riga book witnesses

traditions.label: Mainz Mass-book witnesses
traditions.scope: A medieval summer-part manuscript and one identified Mainz print, not the whole printed series.
traditions.coverage_note: The 1482 book is not made an immediate successor to the Frankfurt manuscript; other dated prints need independent collation.

traditions.label: Olomouc Mass-book witnesses
traditions.scope: Named 1488 print and a surviving fragment of the 1499 print.
traditions.coverage_note: The 1499 fragment cannot characterize the whole edition or demonstrate a new recension.

traditions.label: Augsburg diocesan Missal
traditions.scope: The 1510 Augsburg print, distinct from similarly named Aosta books.
traditions.coverage_note: Earlier and later Augsburg printings require comparison; the title mentions added Masses without dating their introduction.

traditions.label: Bamberg diocesan Missal
traditions.scope: The 1490 Bamberg print identified by its title and colophon.
traditions.coverage_note: Its episcopal preface is indexed, but the instrument and other prints have not been collated.

traditions.label: Bremen diocesan Missal
traditions.scope: The 1511 Bremen print, not a claim about every Bremen manuscript.
traditions.coverage_note: Two fifteenth-century manuscript leads remain uncollated against the print.

traditions.label: Eichstätt diocesan Missal
traditions.coverage_note: The indexed episcopal text and rubrics are bounded contents evidence, not a reviewed reform.

traditions.label: Pécs Mass-book print
traditions.scope: The 1487 Missale Quinqueecclesiense identified in a Wolfenbüttel copy.
traditions.coverage_note: A later handwritten title is explicitly misleading; the 1499 print and fragments remain separate evidence.

traditions.label: Eger-held Mass-book and Eger ordinal
traditions.scope: A dated missal manuscript now held at Eger and a separate 1509 Eger ordinal component.
traditions.coverage_note: Miskolc use is uncertain from the scribe name; an ordinal is not a complete Mass book.

traditions.label: Zadar Franciscan gradual-missal
traditions.scope: A thirteenth-century OFM gradual-missal, separate from a secular Zadar diocesan use.
traditions.coverage_note: The catalogue attribution and manuscript contents support a bounded OFM state, not a diocesan recension.

traditions.label: Split manuscript leads
traditions.scope: The Split cathedral missal, its older sacramentary fragments, and a disputed Dalmatian manuscript attribution.
traditions.coverage_note: No secure single dated Split book-state row is promoted here; layers and origin need examination.

traditions.label: Utrecht diocesan Missal
traditions.scope: The 1495 Delft printing titled for the Utrecht ordinal.
traditions.coverage_note: Other Delft and later prints need collation; Old Catholic reception is outside this witness claim.

traditions.label: Riga Mass-book manuscript
traditions.scope: Akad. Rīga Ms. 1 (R 2665), catalogued as Missale Rigense.
traditions.coverage_note: The c.1450 catalogue dating conflicts with another institutional fourteenth-century account; an exact copying bound is not settled.

sources.title: Usuarium book 560, Missale Rigense

sources.title: BSB 2 Inc.c.a. 2432, Missale Bambergense, Bamberg 1490 (MDZ bsb00079544)
sources.inspection: Original page images viewed 2026-10-21 through the MDZ IIIF service: canvas 19 (episcopal mandate), canvas 20 (dating clause and woodcut), canvases 7–18 (complete calendar, January–December), canvas 5 (blessing of salt and water).
sources.limitations: Selected leaves only; body of the Mass texts not collated. Image numbers are digital canvases, not printed foliation.

sources.title: BSB 2 Inc.c.a. 3784, Missale Bambergense, Bamberg: Johann Pfeyl 1499 (MDZ bsb00030069)
sources.inspection: Original page images viewed 2026-10-21: canvases 7–18 (complete calendar), canvas 19 (fol. I incipit), canvas 604 (colophon), end canvases 601–611.
sources.limitations: No episcopal mandate is present between calendar and fol. I in this copy; Mass bodies not collated.

sources.title: BSB 2 Inc.c.a. 2589, Missale Augustanum, Augsburg: Erhard Ratdolt 1491 (MDZ bsb00043368)
sources.inspection: Canvas 7 (mandate of Bishop Friedrich von Zollern dated Dillingen 10 January 1489, reprinted) and canvas 9 (January calendar) viewed 2026-10-21.
sources.limitations: Reprinted 1489 mandate; this 1491 printing is not admitted as a separate stage. Only January calendar compared.

sources.title: BSB 2 Inc.c.a. 3352, Missale Augustanum, Augsburg: Erhard Ratdolt 1496 (MDZ bsb00030057)
sources.inspection: Canvases 8–9 (new mandate of Bishop Friedrich von Zollern dated Dillingen 10 June 1496) and calendar canvases 10–21 viewed 2026-10-21.
sources.limitations: Mandate statements about restoring the old institution and uniformity are contemporary claims, not collation; Mass bodies not compared.

sources.title: BSB 2 Liturg. 185 a, Missale secundum ritum Augustensis ecclesie, Augsburg: Ratdolt 1510 (MDZ bsb00017896)
sources.inspection: Canvas 3 (title), canvas 5 (mandate of Bishop Heinrich von Lichtenau dated Dillingen 1 February 1510) and calendar canvases 7–18 viewed 2026-10-21. This is the copy indexed as Usuarium book 19.
sources.limitations: The title claim of added Masses and a new Office of the dead was not traced into the body; calendar months compared show no added feasts.

sources.title: BSB Rar. 2102, Liber Missalis secundum ritum ecclesie Augustensis, [Basel] for Christoph Thum 1510 (MDZ bsb00004910)
sources.inspection: Canvas 5 (title), canvases 11–12 (mandate of Bishop Heinrich von Lichtenau naming Christoph Thum, dated Dillingen 1 March 1510, and letter of Caspar Hasslach dated Basel 24 February 1510) and calendar canvases 13–18 viewed 2026-10-21. Canvas 509 (printed fol. CCXXXVIII, end of the book) read 2026-10-22: after a closing section on defects ending 'Laus deo', a red colophon states that the Liber missalis secundum ritum ecclesie Augustensis was made at the command and expense of Christoph Thum, citizen of Augsburg, 'Finit feliciter', with no date, place or printer.
sources.limitations: Printer attribution [Basel] is catalogue-supplied; body texts uncollated.

sources.title: BSB Rar. 2101, Missale secundum ritum Augustensis ecclesie, Dillingen: Sebald Mayer 1555 (MDZ bsb00084486)
sources.inspection: Canvas 5 (title naming Cardinal Otto Truchsess von Waldburg) and canvases 7–8 (undated episcopal mandate, Dillingen) viewed 2026-10-21.
sources.limitations: The mandate describes collation of old missals and additions of Masses, votive orations, rubrics and cautelae; these are claims, not inspected changes. Calendar and body not compared.

sources.title: BSB Rar. 953, Missale Eystetense, Eichstätt: Michael Reyser 1486 (MDZ bsb00032901)
sources.inspection: Canvas 10 (mandate of Bishop Wilhelm von Reichenau) and calendar canvases 3–9 (July–December; January–June leaves not present at the front of this copy) viewed 2026-10-21. On 2026-10-22 canvases 3–6 were viewed again at full size: canvas 3 is a July page partly covered by a colour target; canvas 4 is the same July page unobscured, canvas 5 August and canvas 6 September.
sources.limitations: The mandate gives the year 1486 and the bishop's 23rd year but no day; front calendar is incomplete in this copy.

sources.title: BSB Rar. 954, Missale Eystettense, Eichstätt: Michael Reyser 1494 (MDZ bsb00032906)
sources.inspection: Canvas 4 (woodcut with colophon dated 12 July 1494 naming Bishop Wilhelm von Reichenau and Reyser) and calendar canvases 15–26 (October 24, November 25, December 26) viewed 2026-10-21. July–September calendar canvases 21–23 viewed at full size 2026-10-22.
sources.limitations: Prefatory text on canvases 5–12 not read; body uncollated.

sources.title: BSB Rar. 282, Missale secundum chorum et ritum Eystetensis Ecclesie, Nuremberg: Hieronymus Höltzel 1517 (MDZ bsb00013027)
sources.inspection: Canvas 3 (title), calendar canvases 5–16 and canvas 565 (colophon: consent and mandate of Bishop Gabriel von Eyb, completed 16 July 1517) viewed 2026-10-21. July–September calendar canvases 11–13 viewed at full size 2026-10-22.
sources.limitations: No separate mandate leaf located among front canvases 17–22; body uncollated.

sources.title: BSB Rar. 957, Missale Moguntinum, [Würzburg: Georg Reyser 1482] (MDZ bsb00032958)
sources.inspection: Canvases 7–8 (mandate of Archbishop Diether von Isenburg dated Aschaffenburg, Monday after Laetare 1482) and calendar canvases 9–12 (January–April) viewed 2026-10-21. May and June calendar pages (canvases 13–14) viewed at full size 2026-10-22.
sources.limitations: Printer and place are catalogue-supplied; the dating clause gives the mandate date, not a separate colophon.

sources.title: BSB 2 Inc.s.a. 879 k, Ordo Missalis secundum chorum Moguntinensem, [Strasbourg: Johann Prüss, c.1502–1504] (MDZ bsb00002033)
sources.inspection: Canvas 7 (painted arms), calendar canvases 9–20 (January and April compared), canvas 21 (preparation ordo incipit) viewed 2026-10-21. May and June calendar pages (canvases 13–14) viewed at full size 2026-10-22.
sources.limitations: No dated colophon or mandate inspected; printer and date range are GW/BSB attributions (GW M24569: not before 1502, not after 1504).

sources.title: LBZ Rheinland-Pfalz copy, Missale Olomucense, Bamberg: Sensenschmidt for Drach 1488 (dilibri IIIF 1452963)
sources.inspection: Published IIIF manifest https://www.dilibri.de/i3f/v20/1452963/manifest; canvas 7 (mandate of Bishop John of Olomouc with the chapter), canvas 8 (its conclusion dated Olomouc 31 March 1488) and canvas 9 (January calendar) viewed 2026-10-21.
sources.limitations: The dilibri HTML viewer shows a browser-verification interstitial that was not passed; only the public IIIF endpoint was used. Body not collated.

sources.title: BSB 2 Inc.c.a. 3786 m, Missale Olomucense, Nuremberg: Stuchs 1499, fragment (MDZ bsb00051729)
sources.inspection: All seven canvases viewed 2026-10-21: two damaged leaves foliated CCLXVIII and CCLXXIII with binding remnants.
sources.limitations: Fragment only; no title, colophon, mandate or calendar survives in this copy.

sources.title: Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Reg. lat. 2049 (DigiVatLib IIIF)
sources.inspection: IIIF manifest (922 canvases) acquired 2026-10-21; canvases 3–16 surveyed and canvases 14 (fol. 5v, October) and 15 (fol. 6r, November) of the calendar read.
sources.limitations: Calendar leaves only; the gradual and missal sections and any later layers were not collated.

sources.title: Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Prop. Fide III.125, Missale Traiectense (DigiVatLib IIIF)
sources.inspection: IIIF manifest (553 canvases) acquired 2026-10-21; canvases 3–12 and 538–545 surveyed; canvas 11 (November–December calendar) read.
sources.limitations: GW M24789 assigns this copy to the Snellaert Delft edition of 14 August [1495]; no dated colophon was found on the final canvases inspected, so the bracketed year is not read here.

stages.label: Frankfurt Ms. Barth. 118, summer Missal part
stages.scope: One manuscript summer part only.
stages.witness_label: Frankfurt Ms. Barth. 118, summer Missal part
stages.summary: The 1030–1070 range is a catalogue copying estimate, not duration of Mainz use.

evidence.claim: A Mainz-attributed summer-part missal manuscript is catalogued at Frankfurt.

stages.limitations: No full contents, reception or relationship to later prints established.
stages.reception: Local use and original production site are not independently proved.

stages.label: 1482 Missale Moguntinum, BSB Rar. 0957
stages.scope: Single Mainz print, not the whole series.
stages.summary: The 1482 date belongs to Reyser’s printing; the indexed prefatory item is not treated as an independently verified act.

evidence.claim: The print is identified and indexed with episcopal prefatory text, calendar, temporal, Canon and sanctoral.

evidence.locus: MDZ bsb00032958 canvases 7–8 (mandate dated Aschaffenburg, Monday after Laetare 1482)
evidence.claim: Archbishop Diether states the missal was printed according to the ordinary and register of the Mainz metropolis with expert priests' correction, and marks copies with his and St Martin's insignia.

stages.limitations: Original leaves and the remaining printed series are uncollated.
stages.reception: No 1482 diocesan adoption or direct descent from Ms. Barth. 118 asserted.

stages.label: c.1502–1504 Ordo Missalis secundum chorum Moguntinensem, [Prüss]
stages.scope: Undated Strasbourg print for Mainz; January and April calendar compared with 1482.
stages.witness_label: c.1502–1504 Ordo Missalis secundum chorum Moguntinensem, [Prüss]
stages.summary: An undated Mainz missal attributed to Johann Prüss of Strasbourg (GW: not before 1502, not after 1504). Its April calendar carries seven feasts or observances absent from the 1482 calendar.

evidence.locus: MDZ bsb00002033 canvases 9 and 12 (January, April) and 21
evidence.claim: Calendar pages and preparation incipit inspected; date and printer are attributions.

stages.limitations: Date bounds are a bibliographic attribution, not a dated colophon. The 1486, 1488, 1493 and 1497 Mainz prints are uncollated.
stages.reception: No reception evidence.

stages.label: 1488 Missale Olomucense, Bamberg
stages.scope: One edition-identified print; component contents are not certified.
stages.summary: This is the publication date of the Sensenschmidt/Drach book. Its inspected episcopal mandate is dated 31 March 1488, after the catalogue colophon date of 4 March.

evidence.locus: Digitisation title record, Published and Description fields
evidence.claim: The holding library identifies an Olomouc Missal edition of 4 March 1488, 370 leaves.

evidence.locus: dilibri IIIF canvases 7–8 (mandate, dated Olomouc 31 March 1488) and 9 (calendar)
evidence.claim: Bishop John and the chapter state that existing missals were corrupted and diverged from the church's rubric and order; the printed books, emended according to the old observance, are to be acquired and used instead.

stages.limitations: The print was not collated against Olomouc manuscripts or the later prints.
stages.reception: A title for Olomouc does not date first or universal diocesan use.

stages.label: 1499 Missale Olomucense surviving fragment
stages.scope: Fragmentary sanctoral witness only.
stages.summary: The date identifies the edition; the surviving fragment does not stand for its complete contents.

evidence.locus: Book 122, age, shelfmark, Remark Fragment and p. 4 (268r)
evidence.claim: The Nuremberg Stuchs print is identified by a surviving BSB fragment with a sanctoral entry.
The BSB holding is two damaged leaves foliated CCLXVIII and CCLXXIII.

stages.limitations: The date and single indexed leaf do not prove change from 1488.
stages.reception: No local-use date established.

stages.label: 1510 Missale secundum ritum Augustensis ecclesiae
stages.scope: One 1510 Augsburg book; title-level additions only.
stages.summary: Ratdolt’s print is dated 1510, while introduction dates of its named additions are unknown.

evidence.claim: The named Augsburg print contains indexed episcopal prefatory text, calendar, Ordinary and Mass divisions; title mentions added Masses.

evidence.locus: MDZ bsb00017896 canvas 3 (title) and canvas 5 (mandate dated Dillingen 1 February 1510)
evidence.claim: The title advertises added new Masses and an Office of the dead; Bishop Heinrich commands Ratdolt to print corrected copies consonant with those of his predecessor Friedrich.

stages.limitations: The title’s added-Masses language is not encoded as a before/after transition.
stages.reception: The indexed episcopal preface does not by itself establish dates or extent of diocesan implementation.

stages.label: 1510 Liber Missalis secundum ritum ecclesie Augustensis, for Christoph Thum
stages.scope: A second 1510 Augsburg edition under the same bishop, bibliographically distinct from the Ratdolt edition; textual distinctness not established.
stages.witness_label: 1510 Liber Missalis secundum ritum ecclesie Augustensis, for Christoph Thum
stages.summary: Bishop Heinrich von Lichtenau's mandate of 1 March 1510 entrusts this edition to Christoph Thum; a letter of Caspar Hasslach to the Augsburg priests is dated at Basel on 24 February 1510.

evidence.locus: MDZ bsb00004910 canvas 5 (title), canvases 11–12 (mandate and Hasslach letter) and canvas 509 (colophon)
evidence.claim: Title, mandate naming Thum, the Basel-dated letter and the colophon (made at Thum's command and expense, undated) identify a separate 1510 edition.

stages.limitations: Provisional after cold review: a distinct textual state is not established. The edition was commissioned in the same year and under the same bishop as the Ratdolt edition, and its mandate reuses the general emendation formulary of the 1496 mandate; its text is uncollated against Ratdolt 1510. The 1510 printing year and [Basel] are catalogue attributions: the mandate (1 March 1510) and the Basel-dated letter (24 February 1510) bound the printing from below only, and the colophon, read on 2026-10-22 (canvas 509), names Thum as commissioner but gives no date, place or printer. Upgrading still requires a demonstrated textual difference from the Ratdolt 1510 edition.
stages.reception: No reception evidence.

stages.label: 1555 Missale secundum ritum Augustensis ecclesie, Dillingen
stages.scope: Dillingen edition under Cardinal Otto Truchsess von Waldburg; mandate claims emendation and additions.
stages.witness_label: 1555 Missale secundum ritum Augustensis ecclesie, Dillingen
stages.summary: The title calls the book diligently emended, enlarged and better ordered; the cardinal-bishop's mandate says old missals were collated and corrected by experts and that a number of Masses, votive orations, rubrical cautelae and priestly instructions were newly added, saving the old custom of the Augsburg church.

evidence.claim: Title year 1555 and the mandate's account of collation and additions.

stages.limitations: The described additions are the mandate's claim; no before/after locus has been inspected, so no transition is recorded.
stages.reception: No reception evidence; the mandate is undated within the year.

stages.label: 1496 Missale Augustanum, Ratdolt
stages.scope: One Ratdolt print with a new episcopal mandate; calendar compared with 1491 and 1510.
stages.summary: Bishop Friedrich von Zollern's new mandate of 10 June 1496 commissions Ratdolt to print in a larger type and to restore the old institution of the cathedral, for uniformity across the diocese. Its calendar months compared agree with 1491 and 1510.

evidence.claim: Mandate dated Dillingen 10 June 1496 names Erhard Ratdolt and the purpose of the edition.
The preceding 1491 Ratdolt printing reprints the earlier mandate of 10 January 1489.

stages.limitations: Provisional after cold review: a distinct textual state is not established. The mandate is by the same bishop as the 1489 mandate reprinted in 1491 and repeats its general emendation formula, adding a larger type; it does not specify textual changes. January calendar agrees with 1491; January–April, July and October agree with 1510.
stages.reception: Intended for the churches of the diocese; actual adoption not dated.

stages.label: 1490 Liber missalis Bambergensis
stages.scope: One 1490 Bamberg print.
stages.summary: Its title names Bamberg order, and the index locates a bishop’s prefatory item.

evidence.claim: The Sensenschmidt book is identified by the 1490 colophon and indexed Mass sections.

evidence.locus: MDZ bsb00079544 canvas 19 (mandate) and 20 (dating clause 24 March 1490)
evidence.claim: Bishop Heinrich (Groß von Trockau) states that the diocese's missals were worn or corrupted and deviated from the church's rubrics; with the chapter he had them printed in Bamberg and examined against exemplars.

stages.limitations: No comparison with the 1499 or 1507 print, and no inferred reform.
stages.reception: Printing for the Bamberg church is distinct from proved use in every local parish.

stages.label: 1499 Liber missalis secundum ordinem ecclesie Babenbergensis
stages.scope: One Pfeyl print; calendar collated against 1490; title incipit and colophon inspected.
stages.witness_label: 1499 Liber missalis secundum ordinem ecclesie Babenbergensis
stages.summary: The Bamberg printer Johann Pfeyl completed this missal "secundum ordinem ecclesie Babenbergensis" on 29 May 1499. Its calendar repeats the 1490 sanctoral with two entry changes and new computistical apparatus.

evidence.locus: MDZ bsb00030069 canvas 19 (fol. I incipit) and canvas 604 (colophon)
evidence.claim: The title incipit names the order of the Bamberg church and the colophon dates Pfeyl's printing to 29 May 1499.

stages.limitations: No episcopal mandate appears in this copy; Mass bodies and the 1507 print are uncollated.
stages.reception: Printing for the Bamberg order does not date use in particular churches.

stages.label: 1511 Ordo missalis Bremensis
stages.scope: One edition-identified printed missal.
stages.summary: The 1511 year dates the printing.

evidence.claim: The Strasbourg Beck print names Bremen order and contains indexed temporal, Ordinary, Canon, sanctoral and Common.

stages.limitations: Fifteenth-century Bremen manuscripts and this print remain uncollated.
stages.reception: No date of Bremen-wide reception inferred.

stages.label: 1486 Missale Eystetense
stages.scope: One 1486 Eichstätt print.
stages.summary: The date marks publication of BSB Rar. 0953.

evidence.claim: The Reyser print is identified with indexed diocesan prefatory text, Ordinary, sanctoral and local rubrics.
Bishop Wilhelm von Reichenau ordered the missals copied from an exemplar, emended and renewed in 1486, his 23rd year, printed by Reyser, with short cautelae annexed.

stages.limitations: The bishop’s text is an indexed item, not an inspected full instrument; no precursor comparison.
stages.reception: No first-use or later replacement date established.

stages.label: 1494 Missale Eystettense, Reyser
stages.scope: Second Reyser print under Bishop Wilhelm von Reichenau; October–December calendar compared.
stages.summary: The colophon below the episcopal woodcut dates Reyser's printing at Eichstätt to 12 July 1494, at Bishop Wilhelm's expense. Its October calendar adds two entries absent in 1486.

evidence.claim: Dated colophon and calendar pages inspected.

stages.limitations: Prefatory text and Mass bodies not read.
stages.reception: No reception evidence.

stages.label: 1517 Missale secundum chorum et ritum Eystetensis Ecclesie, Höltzel
stages.scope: Nuremberg edition under Bishop Gabriel von Eyb; calendar compared with 1486 and 1494.
stages.witness_label: 1517 Missale secundum chorum et ritum Eystetensis Ecclesie, Höltzel
stages.summary: Hieronymus Höltzel printed this missal by consent and mandate of Bishop Gabriel von Eyb and completed it on 16 July 1517. Its calendar adds Wolfgang on 31 October.

evidence.claim: Title and colophon date the edition and name the bishop's mandate.

stages.limitations: Body uncollated; the 1556 lead remains unexamined.
stages.reception: No reception evidence.

stages.label: 1487 Missale Quinqueecclesiense, Wolfenbüttel copy
stages.scope: One 1487 print despite its later misleading handwritten label.
stages.summary: The source expressly warns that the later Ultramontanorum tag is incorrect.

evidence.locus: Book 91, age, remark and contents pp. 19, 253, 267, 392
evidence.claim: The Basel Wenssler print is attributed to Pécs, with indexed temporal, Ordinary, Canon and sanctoral material.

stages.limitations: Original print has not been collated with 1499 or manuscript fragments.
stages.reception: Attribution of the book is not proof of every parish’s use.

stages.label: Eger U2 VI.5, 1394 missal manuscript
stages.scope: Dated manuscript identity, not a certified Miskolc or Eger local recension.
stages.summary: The year is a scribal colophon date reported by the catalogue.

evidence.locus: Book 764, colophon Remark and contents pp. 18, 164, 170, 242, 367
evidence.claim: A colophon names scribe Ladislaus de Miskolch and year 1394; the manuscript is held at Eger.

stages.limitations: The scribe name alone does not determine production or use place.
stages.reception: Eger holding does not establish historical Eger diocesan reception.

stages.label: 1509 Ordinarius Agriensis component
stages.scope: Ordinal component only.
stages.summary: Its 1509 date is publication, while the modern Dobszay edition is separate.

evidence.locus: Book 854, original title, genre, age and holding fields
evidence.claim: The Haller print is identified as an Eger ordinal for observance, distinct from a missal.

stages.limitations: Exact Mass-specific provisions and relation to 1514 print not checked here.
stages.reception: Title’s Eger association does not give implementation date.

stages.label: BAV Reg. lat. 2049, Zadar OFM gradual-missal
stages.scope: One Franciscan manuscript, not a Zadar cathedral missal.
stages.witness_label: BAV Reg. lat. 2049, Zadar OFM gradual-missal
stages.summary: The range is estimated copying date, not duration of Franciscan use.

evidence.claim: The manuscript is indexed as a gradual and missal with a Roman-curial order title and Mass components in Franciscan Zadar context.

The calendar is of Roman-curial type: Francis (4 October) in the main hand; the dedication of the Saviour's basilica (9 November) in black and that of Peter and Paul (18 November) in red; Elizabeth with Pontianus (19 November) and an October entry are added in a later hand. Chrysogonus (24 November), Zadar's patron, appears only as the ordinary Roman entry in black, and no October or November entry is marked as specific to Zadar.

stages.limitations: Original leaves and possible later layers are uncollated.
stages.reception: The OFM attribution does not establish a separate secular Zadar recension.

stages.label: 1495 Missale secundum ordinarium Traiectensem
stages.scope: One identified Delft edition.
stages.summary: The 1495 date is a print date, not a new Utrecht rite event.

evidence.claim: The Snellaert Delft print names the Utrecht ordinal and is indexed with the major Mass divisions and colophon.
A second copy assigned by GW to the same edition carries Utrecht calendar entries: Willibrord (7 November), Lebuinus (12 November), Radbod with vigil (29 November) and Martin (11 November).

stages.limitations: Other Utrecht manuscripts and prints remain uncollated.
stages.reception: No relation to modern Old Catholic books or adoption date is asserted.

stages.label: Akad. Rīga Ms. 1 (R 2665), Missale Rigense
stages.date_label: c.1450 catalogue estimate; competing fourteenth-century dating unresolved
stages.scope: One manuscript with reported provenance and marginal notes.
stages.summary: The catalogue identifies one Riga missal with indexed Mass contents and a reported cathedral altar ownership note. Its copying date is left unpositioned pending reconciliation of divergent estimates.

evidence.locus: Book 560, age, shelfmark, fol. 2 note and contents pp. 4, 10, 209, 214, 281
evidence.claim: The catalogue identifies one Riga missal with indexed Mass contents and a reported cathedral altar ownership note.

stages.limitations: Ownership transcription and manuscript layers need original-folio review; this is not the Viborg print held in Riga.
stages.reception: The altar note is ownership context, not an independently established date of general Riga adoption.

transitions.summary: Between the 1490 and 1499 Bamberg prints the calendar changes at two entries and gains computistical apparatus; the remaining sanctoral, grading and vigils agree on all twelve month pages.

changes.before: 18 December (xv kal. Jan.): Wunibald titled confessor and bishop.
1 July: Gaius pope with a vigil marked.
changes.after: 1 July: Gaius pope without the vigil.

changes.before: No computistical keys, bissextile locus, dog-day or Prisca Alleluia notes.
changes.after: Adds Easter and movable-feast keys, the bissextile locus at 24 February, the equinox rule at 21 March, dog days at 14 July, and a note at Prisca (18 January) that Alleluia is never laid aside before Prisca's day ("Ante diem Prisce nunquam deponitur alleluia").

transitions.limitations: Calendar only, compared by eye page by page; spelling variation ignored. No body, Canon or Ordinary comparison. Direct derivation of 1499 from 1490 is not claimed.

transitions.summary: The 1494 Eichstätt calendar omits Praxedis on 21 July and adds a translation of St Walburga on 12 October and a vigil on 31 October; July–December otherwise agree.
transitions.limitations: Only July–December were compared (the 1486 copy lacks January–June); August, September, November and December agree. Bodies uncollated. Absence from one calendar page does not prove absence from the sanctorale.

transitions.summary: Between 1494 and 1517 the Eichstätt calendar gains the octave of the Visitation (9 July), Christopher (25 July), the Transfiguration (6 August), the octave of the Nativity of Mary (15 September) and Wolfgang beside the All Saints vigil (31 October).

changes.after: 25 July: Jacobi apostoli with Christoferi martyris.

changes.before: 6 August: Sixti, Felicissimi et Agapiti martyrum only.
changes.after: 6 August: Sixti, Felicissimi et Agapiti with Transfiguratio domini.
15 September: Octaua Natiuitatis Marie with Nicomedis martyris.

transitions.limitations: July–December only; January–June and the bodies are uncollated, and no intermediate edition is compared, so the date at which each entry was added within 1494–1517 is unknown. Linus (26 November) is printed in black in both 1494 and 1517; the 1517 page only prefixes a red paragraph mark, whose meaning is not established, so it is not counted as a calendar change.

transitions.summary: The calendar of the Prüss Mainz missal names further saints at dates left blank in the 1482 calendar: seven entries in April, six in May and six in June; January agrees.

changes.before: April: entries only for Ambrose (4), Mary of Egypt (9), Tiburtius and Valerian (14), George (23), Mark (25), Vitalis (28), Peter Martyr (29), Quirinus (30).
changes.after: April adds Florentius (3), Celestine pope (6), Adalarius bishop (20), Adalbert beside George (23), Wendelin (24), Litania maior beside Mark (25), and Cletus and Marcellinus (26).

changes.before: May: 2 May blank; 4 May Festum corone spinee only; 8, 9, 19 and 30 May blank.
changes.after: May adds Walpertus bishop (2), Florianus martyr beside the Crown of Thorns (4), the Revelation of St Michael (8), the Translation of St Nicholas (9), Ivo confessor and Potentiana virgin (19) and Felix pope and martyr (30, iii kal. Iun.).

changes.before: June: Erasmus alone on 3 June; 6, 8, 13, 14 and 20 June blank.
changes.after: June adds Morandus confessor beside Erasmus (3), Claudius archbishop (6), Medard bishop (8), Onuphrius confessor (13), Basil bishop (14) and Deodatus bishop (20, xii kal. Jul.).

transitions.limitations: The four intervening Mainz incunable editions are uncollated, so the edition that introduced these entries is unknown. Only January and April–June were compared; spelling differences are ignored.

gaps.missing: The 1482 mandate is read and its January and April–June calendar compared with the c.1502–1504 Prüss print (additions in April, May and June); the Frankfurt manuscript, the 1486–1497 prints, July–December and all later editions remain uncollated.
gaps.next_source: Frankfurt Ms. Barth. 118 images; Mainz prints 1486 (Berlin), c.1488 (WLB Stuttgart), 1493 (Darmstadt/Weimar), 1497 to locate the introducing edition; July–December canvases 15–20 of MDZ bsb00032958 and bsb00002033.
gaps.consequence: One calendar revision is documented across an unresolved run of editions; no manuscript-to-print descent is asserted.

gaps.missing: The 1488 mandate (31 March 1488) is read; the 1499 BSB holding is confirmed as two leaves only. Manuscripts and the 1505/1712/1740 books remain uncollated.

The Basel 1510 colophon (MDZ bsb00004910 canvas 509) is read and is undated, so its 1510 date and Basel place remain attributions.
gaps.next_source: MDZ bsb00030055 (1489), paired Mass bodies and appended Masses in bsb00017896, bsb00004910 and bsb00084486.
gaps.consequence: Edition sequence and episcopal claims are recorded; no Augsburg text revision is documented.

gaps.missing: The 1490/1499 calendars are collated and the 1490 mandate is read; the 1507 print, the 1499 front matter beyond the calendar, and all Mass bodies remain uncollated.

January–June of 1494/1517, the 1494 prefatory text, the bodies and the 1556 lead remain.
